title: The House of Cold Spring
premise: Tamsin Galloway takes a teaching post at Cold Spring Academy, a remote school where one student vanishes from every graduating class and no one will say why. When Tamsin's sleep-study recordings capture a second voice answering questions in their own cadence, they learn the founders bound something beneath the school with a ritual that must be renewed each harvest moon—and this year, the chosen vessel is Tamsin. Refusing to believe, then unable not to, Tamsin uncovers that the missing students were never lost but fed to the house's memory, which keeps them alive as echoes. In the end, Tamsin completes the founders' interrupted final rite—not to renew the bargain, but to sever it—freeing the echoes and paying for survival with their own memories of the school, walking out at dawn knowing only that they must never come back.
about_author: Sebastian Vane is the pen name of a former boarding-school caretaker who spent eleven years in buildings older than the towns around them. They write horror about institutions that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: The Long Drive Up
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Arriving at Cold Spring Academy through fog-thick pines, Tamsin notes small wrongnesses: no birds, a gate that latches itself. The headmistress, Mrs. Aldous, is warm but evasive. Emotional beat: cautious optimism curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. First day teaching; the class is bright, obedient, strangely synchronized. A girl named Wren asks why the register has twenty names when nineteen desks sit empty. Emotional beat: professional composure masking the first real crack of dread.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldous hands over a laminated list of rules—no recording after midnight, no entering the east wing, no answering if called by name after dark. Tamsin laughs it off. Emotional beat: wry skepticism establishing the skeptic's armor.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Reviewing archives, Tamsin finds a pattern: one student per year, unremarked, unreported, going back a century. Colleague Mr. Fenwick warns them to stop looking. Emotional beat: investigative thrill shadowed by institutional menace.

chapters.title: Sleep Study
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Insomnia drives Tamsin into the school's old sleep clinic, now a wellness room, where they begin recording their nights as a joke experiment. First night: nothing. Second night: static shaped like breathing. Emotional beat: loneliness turning toward obsession.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Playback reveals a voice answering questions Tamsin asked aloud in sleep—answering correctly, in Tamsin's own intonation. It says: 'You're late.' Emotional beat: terror breaking through disbelief.

chapters.title: Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The quiet girl corners Tamsin, revealing she hears it too—that her sister was 'taken' two years ago and everyone pretends otherwise. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, grief under discipline.

chapters.title: East Wing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Breaking the rule, Tamsin enters the sealed east wing and finds the founders' chapel: a circle of chairs, a ledger of names, and a wall of children's drawings all depicting the same door. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The ledger records a ritual begun in 1897 and left unfinished—the founders died mid-rite, leaving the thing below half-bound, hungry, negotiating. Each harvest moon, the school feeds it a name to keep the seal holding. Emotional beat: horrified comprehension of the price of survival.

chapters.title: Called by Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At night the voice uses Tamsin's full name, learned from the ledger. Doors open on their own floors. Tamsin nearly answers. Emotional beat: erosion of the skeptic's armor; belief arrives unwanted.

chapters.title: What Aldous Carries
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The headmistress remembers her own harvest moon forty years ago, when she was spared because someone else volunteered. She has kept the school running out of guilt, not malice. Emotional beat: antagonist revealed as fellow survivor.

chapters.title: The Echoes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leads Tamsin to the cellar where the taken students persist as echoes—memories given form, repeating their last days. Among them, her sister, who begs Wren not to finish what the founders started. Emotional beat: heartbreak complicating the mission.

chapters.title: Two Rituals
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Deciphering the chapel texts, Tamsin finds the founders' rite has two endings: renewal (feed it, keep surviving) or severance (unmake it, lose what the house holds—including memories). Emotional beat: the theme crystallized as an impossible choice.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Three days to the moon. The house grows bold: hallways rearrange, clocks run backward, students sleepwalk toward the cellar. Aldous begins preparing the renewal rite. Emotional beat: countdown pressure, allies fracturing.

chapters.title: Fenwick's Bargain
chapters.summary: Fenwick's POV. The colleague confesses he was meant to be taken years ago and bought his life by recruiting replacements ever since. He offers Tamsin the same deal. Emotional beat: self-loathing; the seduction of survival at another's cost.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The voice appears wearing Tamsin's face and offers a third path: become part of the house willingly, keep your memories, keep Wren safe forever. Tamsin almost says yes. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: What Wren Won't Lose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren refuses to let Tamsin trade themselves, revealing her sister's echo whispered the truth: severance frees the echoes but erases the house from every mind that knew it—including hers. She chooses freedom over remembering. Emotional beat: sacrificial love, devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin writes letters they won't remember writing, memorizes Wren's face, and prepares the severance rite with Aldous, who finally chooses to help undo her life's grim stewardship. Emotional beat: quiet resolve before catastrophe.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Under the risen moon, Aldous begins the renewal rite as cover while Tamsin works the severance in the chapel. The house fights back—flooding halls with borrowed memories, screaming in the voices of every taken child. Emotional beat: climax, chaos, cost mounting.

chapters.title: Severance
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. To complete the rite, Tamsin must give the house its final meal: their own living memory of Cold Spring. They speak the closing words the founders never finished. The door in the children's drawings opens—and closes. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Dawn, Empty-Handed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes at the bus stop with no sister, no school, no reason she came here—only a name written on her palm: Tamsin. A stranger beside her doesn't know why they're crying. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; memory as the final payment.

chapters.title: The House of Cold Spring
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, fragmented. Driving away at dawn, Tamsin finds a child's drawing on the passenger seat—a door, closed—and cannot explain the ache of relief. Somewhere behind, the pines stand silent, and for the first time in a century, nothing answers when called. Emotional beat: haunted peace; survival's price paid in full.
